assessment.rationale: No one cures macular degeneration, so the Main KPI of 196,000,000 patients cured is open work, though what exists must be stated honestly. The two approved geographic-atrophy drugs only slow lesion growth, by about 16 to 22 percent (pegcetacoplan) and 14 to 28 percent (avacincaptad pegol), with little change in best-corrected or low-luminance acuity, vision-function benefit only in post hoc analyses, repeated intravitreal injections and increased risk of progression to wet disease (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=%22geographic%20atrophy%22%20AND%20%28pegcetacoplan%20OR%20avacincaptad%29%20AND%20%28outcomes%20OR%20%22visual%20function%22%29&format=json&pageSize=5&resultType=core). Gene therapy targets injection burden rather than cure, with ABBV-RGX-314 the only phase 2-3 programme (671 participants) among otherwise phase 1 and 1-2 cell and gene studies, including autologous iPSC-RPE in 10 patients and hESC-RPE in 16; none is approved. Photoreceptor and RPE replacement remains unproven: a 2026 PNAS study states functional visual gains from iPSC-derived RPE are modest to date, and reviews cite poor cell survival and integration. Open source is two small image-classification repositories (https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=macular+degeneration+OCT+deep+learning&per_page=10&sort=stars). Honest limit: anti-VEGF and complement inhibition are standard care and thoroughly published, so tasks on them are known answers; the open work is restoring lost photoreceptor and RPE function, which no approved or open solution does.

additionalSearches.query: approved geographic atrophy drugs and visual function
additionalSearches.finding: 2026 reviews: pegcetacoplan and avacincaptad pegol are the only FDA-approved options for geographic atrophy and slow lesion growth by about 16-22 and 14-28 percent versus sham, with little improvement in best-corrected or low-luminance acuity, vision benefits only from post hoc analyses, repeated injections, and increased risk of progression to wet AMD. Patients and physicians describe treatment as delaying progression without restoring vision.

additionalSearches.query: registered cell and gene therapy trials in macular degeneration
additionalSearches.finding: The only late-stage entry is ABBV-RGX-314 subretinal gene therapy for neovascular AMD, phase 2-3 with 671 participants, active not recruiting; everything else is phase 1, 1-2 or early phase 1, including autologous iPSC-RPE transplantation in 10 patients, hESC-RPE subretinal implantation in 16, retinal stem and progenitor cells in 20, and several nAMD gene therapies with 10 to 48 participants. Nothing approved.

No trial-level restoration of vision appears. A 2026 PNAS study of the human RPE 3D epigenomic landscape states that functional visual gains achieved to date with iPSC-derived RPE are modest; 2026 reviews of stem-cell retinal restoration cite poor cell survival and integration; a Cell Reports Medicine review cites the 2014 RPE graft as a milestone without outcome data.
Two repositories (1 and 0 stars) doing OCT-based AMD classification and fundus segmentation. Open source addresses detection, not treatment, so no open solution cures or reverses the disease.
